title: Jotham's Fable of the Trees
text:
Abimelech, a son of the judge Gideon, wanted to rule over Shechem. With money from the local temple he hired men, went to his father's house and killed his brothers, seventy of them, on a single stone. Only the youngest, Jotham, escaped by hiding. The citizens of Shechem then made Abimelech king.

When Jotham heard, he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim above the town and called down a fable. Once the trees went out to anoint a king. They asked the olive tree, but it said it would not give up its oil, which honored gods and men, just to sway over the trees. They asked the fig tree, which would not leave its sweet fruit, and the vine, which would not leave the wine that cheered gods and men. Finally they asked the bramble. The bramble accepted and said: come and take shelter in my shade, and if not, let fire come out of the bramble and burn up the cedars of Lebanon.

Jotham told the Shechemites that if they had acted in good faith, they could rejoice in their king, and if not, fire would come from Abimelech and consume them. Then he fled. Three years later Abimelech and Shechem turned on each other, he destroyed the town, and he died besieging another.
lesson: When capable people refuse responsibility because they are comfortable, it often falls to whoever wants it most. Ask who is eager for power and why, and do not leave the field to them.
people: Jotham, Abimelech, the citizens of Shechem
place: Tell Balata (ancient Shechem), Nablus, West Bank
